page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL4 is an x86_64 architecture server virtualized via the KVM hypervisor. The system features 16 vCPUs configured with a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU.

The primary hardware differentiator is the inclusion of three NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture family, providing a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM. This server does not include any local storage, meaning external storage volumes must be attached to handle data persistence. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From a resource density perspective, this configuration offers a high ratio of GPU accelerators and system memory relative to the vCPU count. However, the shared CPU allocation model represents a potential performance tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, non-burstable CPU processing. The lack of local storage also requires architectural planning for disk I/O.

This server is designed for workloads that leverage GPU acceleration and high memory capacity, such as machine learning inference, data science jobs, and parallel graphics processing, while being less dependent on dedicated, continuous CPU cores or local disk storage.
